electron-configuration-s1.title: Four pairs of charged particles
electron-configuration-s1.text: Each row shows two charged particles a distance apart. Charges are in units of the proton's charge; distances are in picometers (pm).

items.q: According to Coulomb's law, which pair attracts each other most strongly?
options: Pair S
Pair P
Pair Q
Pair R

why.correct: F ∝ q₁q₂/r². In units of P's force: P = 1, Q = 2, R = 1/4, S = 4/4 = 1. Q is strongest.
options: S has the largest product of charges (4), but twice the distance cuts the force by 4, so it ties with P.
P is half as strong as Q, which has double the charge at the same distance.
Right: q₁q₂/r² = (2)(1)/200² is the largest: twice pair P's value.
Same charges as P at twice the distance: one quarter of P's force, the weakest.

items.q: How does the force in pair R compare with the force in pair P?
options: One quarter as strong
Half as strong
Twice as strong
The same strength, since the charges match

why.correct: F ∝ 1/r²: twice the distance gives (1/2)² = 1/4 of the force.
options: Right: doubling the distance divides the force by 2² = 4.
Force falls with the square of distance, not the distance itself.
A larger distance weakens the attraction.
Matching charges, but the distance doubled, so the force changes.

items.q: A student claims pair S attracts most strongly because it has the largest charges. Which reply best uses the data?
options: The student is right; charge outweighs distance in Coulomb's law
S is the weakest, because its charges are the most spread out
S is not comparable with the others, since both its charges are 2
S has 4 times P's charges but twice the distance, so S equals P
Distance is squared, so it matters at least as much as charge.
S is not the weakest: R, with smaller charges at the same distance, is.
Coulomb's law compares any pairs using the product of charges and the distance.
Right: both the charges and the distance matter, and here they cancel.

items.q: The potential energy of two opposite charges is proportional to q₁q₂/r. Which pair would need the least energy to pull apart?
options: Pair P
Pair R
Pair Q
Pair S

why.correct: Potential energy depends on q₁q₂/r (one power of r). P 1/200, Q 2/200, R 1/400, S 4/400. R is the least strongly bound.
options: P: 1/200, twice R's value, so separating it takes more energy.
Right: R has the smallest |q₁q₂|/r, 1/400, so its potential energy is the least negative.
Q: 2/200, the largest attraction (tied with S), so it takes the most energy to separate.
S: 4/400 = 2/200, tied with Q for the most energy needed.

items.q: What is the electron configuration of sulfur (16 electrons)?
options: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶
1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴
1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 2d⁶
1s² 2s⁶ 2p⁸

why.correct: Fill in energy order: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴. The superscripts add to 16.
options: This holds 18 electrons, which is argon.
Right: 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 4 = 16 electrons, filled in order of energy.
There is no 2d subshell; the second shell has only s and p.
An s subshell holds at most 2 electrons and a p subshell 6.

items.q: Which is the electron configuration of iron (26 electrons) in noble gas notation?
options: [Ar] 3d⁸
[Ar] 4s² 4d⁶
[Kr] 4s² 3d⁶
[Ar] 4s² 3d⁶

why.correct: Argon (18) + 4s² + 3d⁶ = 26. The 3d subshell fills after 4s in the neutral atom.
options: The 4s subshell is lower in energy than 3d in a neutral atom, so it fills first.
After 4s comes 3d, not 4d. The d subshell is one shell behind.
Krypton has 36 electrons, more than iron has in total.
Right: 18 electrons in the argon core, then 4s fills before 3d: 2 + 6 = 8 more.

items.q: What is the electron configuration of the Fe²⁺ ion?
options: [Ar] 3d⁶
[Ar] 4s² 3d⁴
[Ar] 4s² 3d⁸
[Ar] 4s¹ 3d⁵

why.correct: Fe is [Ar] 4s² 3d⁶. Remove the two 4s electrons (outermost shell) to get Fe²⁺: [Ar] 3d⁶.
options: Right: an ion loses electrons from the highest shell first, which is the 4s.
The 4s electrons, in shell 4, are farther out and are removed before 3d.
A positive ion has fewer electrons than the atom, not more.
Both lost electrons come from 4s; none come from 3d first.

items.q: How many valence electrons does an atom of phosphorus, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³, have?

mistakes.why: Value: count the whole outer shell, both 3s and 3p: 2 + 3 = 5.
Value: that is all the electrons. Valence electrons are only those in the outermost shell.

why.correct: Valence electrons are in the outermost shell, n = 3: 3s² 3p³ gives 2 + 3 = 5.

items.q: It takes more energy to remove the outermost electron from lithium than from sodium. Which explanation is best?
options: Sodium is a bigger atom, so it has a weaker hold on each of its electrons
Lithium has fewer protons, so it holds its electron more tightly
Sodium's valence electron is in shell 3, farther out, behind 10 core electrons
Sodium has more mass, which makes its electrons easier to remove

why.correct: Lithium's 2s electron is close to the nucleus behind 2 core electrons. Sodium's 3s electron is in a farther shell behind 10 core electrons, so it is held less tightly.
options: "Bigger" needs a cause; name the outer shell (3 vs 2) and the core electrons.
Fewer protons would mean a weaker pull; something else must outweigh that.
Right: more distance and more shielding outweigh sodium's extra protons.
Mass does not appear in Coulomb's law; charge and distance do.

items.q: Neon has fewer protons than sodium, yet removing neon's outermost electron takes about four times as much energy. Which explanation fits Coulomb's law?
options: Neon's outer electron is in shell 2, closer, behind just 2 core electrons
Neon is a gas, and electrons are harder to remove from gases
Neon has a full shell, which wants to stay full
Sodium has more electrons, so it can spare one more easily

why.correct: Neon's 2p electron feels 10 protons shielded by only 2 core electrons, at a small distance. Sodium's 3s electron feels 11 protons through 10 core electrons, much farther out.
options: Right: sodium's 3s electron is farther away and behind 10 core electrons.
Every atom here is studied as a gas; the state is not the cause.
Atoms do not want things; the reason is distance and shielding.
The energy depends on how strongly that electron is attracted, not on how many there are.

items.q: How many core electrons does sodium have?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the valence electron. Core electrons are the inner ones, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶.

why.correct: Core electrons are those in the inner shells: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ = 10. Sodium has 11 electrons, 1 of them valence.

items.q: Which statements about the three atoms are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Lithium and sodium each have one valence electron
Neon's valence shell is n = 2
Sodium's valence electron is in a p subshell
Lithium has more core electrons than sodium

why.correct: Valence electrons are in the outermost shell: Li 1 (2s¹), Na 1 (3s¹), Ne 8 (2s² 2p⁶).
options: Right: 2s¹ and 3s¹.
Right: its outermost electrons are in 2s and 2p.
It is in 3s.
Lithium has 2 core electrons; sodium has 10.

items.q: Put these subshells in the order they fill in a neutral atom, lowest energy first.
options: 2p
3s
3p
4s
3d
4p

why.correct: The aufbau order continues 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p. 4s fills before 3d because in neutral atoms its energy is lower.

items.q: Moving from an electron in a 2p subshell to an electron in a 3p subshell of the same atom, predict how each quantity changes.

variables.name: Average distance from the nucleus
variables.why: Shell 3 is farther from the nucleus than shell 2.

variables.name: Energy needed to remove that electron
variables.why: A farther electron is attracted less strongly, so it takes less energy to remove.

variables.name: Number of protons in the nucleus
variables.why: Both electrons belong to the same atom.

why.correct: Same nucleus, larger distance: weaker attraction, higher (less negative) energy, easier to remove.

items.q: How many electrons can one p subshell hold?

why.correct: s holds 2, p holds 6, d holds 10: two electrons per orbital, with 1, 3 and 5 orbitals.
options: Right: three orbitals of 2 electrons each.
That is an s subshell, with one orbital.
That is a d subshell, with five orbitals.
A whole shell n = 2 holds 8 (2s and 2p together), but one p subshell holds 6.
